relationships.description: The layout configuration is linked to a reusable library component as its default or recommended arrangement of that component's slotted children, without either owning the other.
relationships.evidence: The library component's definition file references the layout config by id (e.g. a defaultLayout or layout field), or the layout config lists the component among the types it is intended for.

relationships.description: A parent layout configuration embeds a nested layout configuration, such as a grid area's inner flex rules, that exists only as part of the enclosing arrangement and is discarded with it.
relationships.evidence: The parent layout's spec contains the child layout inline as a nested object (e.g. an areas or regions entry holding its own display/gap/alignment properties) rather than referencing a separately defined layout.

relationships.description: The layout configuration sets the binding arrangement rules (layout mode, grid tracks, spacing, width limits) that the view's top-level children must follow when positioned on that surface.
relationships.evidence: The view's spec declares a layout reference to the config, and the rendered page's root container carries the config's CSS grid/flex, gap and max-width values.

relationships.description: The layout configuration supplies the container arrangement a sub-view uses to position its grouped component instances within the parent view's region.
relationships.evidence: The sub-view definition (inline or via its LibrarySubView) has a layout property pointing to the config, and the sub-view's wrapper element applies the config's display, gap and alignment styles.

relationships.description: The layout configuration supplies the arrangement scheme the view applies to position its component instances and sub-views on the surface.
relationships.evidence: The view's spec file references the layout config by id in its layout field, and the generated view template wraps its children in a container styled with that config's properties.

notes: governs and provides between LayoutConfig and View express essentially the same fact (the view uses this layout); keep one, preferably 'applies' from the ux category, which fits better than either. 'applies' would likewise suit SubView instead of provides.
